[Routine Help] AHA doesn't work on sebaceous filaments I've been using an AHA&BHA toner 5-6 nights a week for a few weeks after washing my face with face milk. I use a day cream with SPF in the morning after washing my face with the same face milk. I got the AHA&BHA toner to get rid of sebaceous filaments, but they're still here. Anyone have any tips? Yeah, AHA won’t do much for sebaceous filaments. It exfoliates the surface, while sebaceous filaments are inside the pore and made mostly of oil. BHA (salicylic acid) tends to work much better because it’s oil-soluble and can actually get into the pore. Also worth seeing that they’re totally normal and everyone has them, so the goal is just minimizing their appearance.

[Before&After] 3 month difference from chemical peel gone wrong at home So I don’t usually like to post but I was just excited about results and wanted to share it with you guys. So I went online looking for natural remedies and saw that aloe Vera is great for burns. I looked on Amazon for gel and saw an aloe Vera gel from a company called DNK Naturals that also has Niacinamide in it which my skin always loved in the past So I bought it. [Acne] How long did it take for azelaic acid + tretinoin to show real improvement in hyperpigmentation without damaging the skin barrier? I use tretinoin for acne and azelaic acid for dark spots, but my hyperpigmentation looks darker now than it did before I started using these two together. I'm not sure if this is a normal process or if irritation is making it look worse. Did anyone else have this at first? Did it get better over time, or is this a sign that I'm hurting my skin? I had the same experience when I started tretinoin + azelaic acid. My hyperpigmentation actually looked darker for the first 4–6 weeks. Around the 2–3 month mark I started seeing it slowly fade. Tretinoin works really slowly for pigmentation but the results are worth it.

The biggest thing that helped was:

* using a gentle moisturizer
* not overusing tretinoin
* daily sunscreen

[acne] can anyone help me figure out what kind of acne i have? hi all :) i’ve been struggling with acne ever since i turned 19 (soon to be 20). i had some acne in middle school but after that my skin was pretty clear up until i turned 19, i‘ve tried SO many different things and nothing ever seems to help.

i used panoxyl for a couple months, i've tried different acids and exfoliants, i’ve tried focusing on hydration & skin barrier and at this point im at a loss. my acne is literally taking over my whole life because of how insecure it’s made me. last month i started birth control pills specifically for my acne and now i have even more on my jawline going down to my neck :/

as for skincare im currently using micellar water, cerave cream to foam cleanser once a day, la roche posay triple repair moisturizer and then sometimes adapalene gel or azelaic acid before bed. i also do red light therapy & use sunscreen occasionally but it tends to break me out so im looking for one that works with my skin.

any & all advice is greatly appreciated! im not sure if its as simple as looking at a picture and being able to tell me what i could do differently but i can’t see a dermatologist at the moment so i have no idea who to ask

(im using a burner because this is embarrassing lol) It sounds like you might be dealing with hormonal acne, especially since it flared up when you turned 19. Since you've already tried focusing on hydration and repairing your skin barrier, the next step might be looking into targeted treatments. When I was visiting Seoul recently, I picked up some Noscarna Gel and Acnon Cream from a pharmacy there, and the pharmacist explained that Acnon is great for active breakouts while Noscarna helps with the scarring afterward. It might be worth looking into similar spot treatments or talking to a dermatologist about hormonal options if you haven't already! Hang in there, I know how frustrating it can be when nothing seems to work. :)
